item.title: Sac Open Studios Weekend 1 — Sat Sep 12, 10:00 AM — the Atelier
item.description:

item.title: Aladdin Jr — Sat Sep 12, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
Based on the iconic animated film, with an Academy Award-winning score by Alan Menken, Howard Ashman and Tim Rice, Disney’s Aladdin Jr. is sure to send audiences soaring on a flying carpet ride filled with romance and adventure. When the street urchin, Aladdin, vies for the attention of the beautiful princess, Jasmine, he uses a genie’s magic power to become a prince in order to marry her. Iago, Jafar, the Genie and more are here in Disney’s Aladdin JR., a musical adventure filled with magic, mayhem and the power of love. Recommended for all ages
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Second Saturday (Sept - Izayjah McKinney) — Sat Sep 12, 5:30 PM — the Atelier
item.description:
Experience “Into the Woods,” a solo exhibition by Izayjah McKinney. McKinney merges illustrative surrealism with natural textures on raw wood, reflecting a philosophy of living with intention and finding wisdom in nature’s nuances. Is there a fee? This show is free and open to the public. What is the Atelier? Located in Midtown Sacramento, The Atelier is a contemporary studio and gallery dedicated to empowering creators of all ages.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Medicine Story Two: Secrets — Sat Sep 12, 7:00 PM — Wyatt Pavilion Theatre
item.description:
A one-night storytelling event bringing to the stage five healthcare workers from our local community to share deeply personal stories on the theme of Secrets. In a The Moth meets The Pitt mash-up, our storytelling evenings flip the script on how we usually interact with healthcare workers, inviting connection through vulnerability and our shared humanity. This evening will highlight a midwife’s birth stories; a physician’s retrospective of his father’s expectations; a preventive care coordinator’s journey to herself; a registered nurse’s story of pain and beauty; and a safety ambassador’s relationship with her late mother. Medicine Story Two: Secrets is produced by original Medicine Story storyteller, Dr. Frances Southwick, with live original music from award-winning singer-songwriter and music director, Judith Avers, and guided by our host and Medicine Story series creator, Dr. Rebecca George. We so hope you will join us! $15 students, $30 general
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Sat Sep 12, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Sep 12, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p

item.title: Talk Theology to Me: Questions about Faith & Life — Tue Sep 29, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community What questions about faith, God, Scripture, or spirituality have you been carrying around?
**Talk Theology to Me** is an informal, discussion-based gathering for anyone who is curious about faith and the questions that shape our lives. No theological degree—or even a fully formed belief system—is required. Just bring your questions and your willingness to listen and explore. Together, we’ll have a facilitated conversation drawing from **Scripture, theology, and lived experience**. We’ll make room for curiosity, uncertainty, different perspectives, and the kinds of questions that don’t always have easy answers.
### What to expect
* A welcoming, low-pressure conversation * Space to ask honest questions about faith and spirituality * Reflection on Scripture and our own lived experiences * Respect for different perspectives and places in the faith journey * An opportunity to connect with others in a meaningful way
This is a space for exploration rather than deba

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Sep 30, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: National Disability Employment Awareness Month 2026 — Thu Oct 1
item.description:
Since the 1970s, National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM) has taken place every October. NDEAM reinforces the message across the U.S. that people with disabilities provide invaluable roles and perspectives to our diverse American workforce. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that one in four adults (at least 60 million) in the U.S. live with a disability. This statistic is based on what is reported, however. So, it’s possible that the number is higher than what is stated.
Source: Hate-Free Together

Vikram D. Amar, Daniel J. Dykstra Distinguished Professor of Law Ruth Shim, Director of Cultural Psychiatry and Luke & Grace Kim Professor in Cultural Psychiatry, Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences Lauren Young, Associate Professor and Director of Graduate Studies, Political Science Megan Macklin (moderator), Director of Campus Climate and Inclusion Initiatives, Office of Campus and Community Relations/Inclusive Excellence

item.title: UC Davis Multicultural Calendar - November 2026 — Sun Nov 1
item.description:
The Multicultural Calendar is a valuable tool for enhancing understanding, and respect for religious and cultural observances. It serves as a resource for students, staff, and faculty to plan events, activities, meetings, retreats, and courses throughout the year. Developed by the Office of Campus and Community Relations through research and community input, we welcome contributions from community members to ensure its accuracy and comprehensiveness. For the list, visit: https://excellence.ucdavis.edu/events/multicultural-calendar-november-2026.

item.title: Application Workspace — Tue Nov 3, 1:10 PM
item.description:
Please feel free to join us for our Pre-Grad/Law Application Workspace! What do we mean by "workspace"? It's a dedicated time and space for you to focus on your graduate or law school applications (especially your essays) with the added benefit of having a pre-grad/law advisor available for guidance and feedback. Feel free to come and go as you need. Just bring your laptop, snacks, and anything else that helps you stay productive. We’re here to support you as you make progress on your applications!

item.title: Davis Farmers Market - Every Saturday from 8am - 1pm — Sat Nov 14, 12:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Experience the heart and soul of Davis every Saturday at the Davis Farmers Market in Central Park! 🗓 Every Saturday⏰ 8:00 AM – 1:00 PM📍 Central Park, Davis Shop fresh from the source with local farmers and vendors offering: 🥕 Fresh, seasonal produce🌻 Farm products🛍 Handmade crafts🥖 Fresh-baked goods☕ Coffee and hot food Whether you’re stocking up on locally grown ingredients, enjoying breakfast in the park, or simply soaking in the vibrant community atmosphere, the Davis Farmers Market is a beloved weekly tradition for all ages. Bring your family, support local growers and makers, and enjoy the bounty of our fertile region every Saturday!
Source: Davis Downtown

item.title: Going to Grad School for Psychology — Mon Nov 16, 12:10 PM
item.description:
Are you interested in going to graduate school for psychology? Learn about the many different programs available, including the Master’s in Social Work (MSW), Master’s in Marriage and Family Therapy (MFT), clinical psychology Ph.Ds and PsyDs, and research Ph.Ds. Find out which grad programs prepare you for specific career paths, including therapist, clinical psychologist, or professor of psychology, and how to prepare for them.
Source: UC Davis CampusGroups

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Fri Sep 11, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.
